sanskrit: tato 'ṅgadavacaḥ śrutvā sarve te vānarottamāḥ svaṃ svaṃ gatau samutsāham āhus tatra yathākramam
english: Then, having heard the words of Aṅgada, all those foremost of monkeys declared, each in turn, their own eagerness and capacity for the journey.

sanskrit: gajo gavākṣo gavayaḥ śarabho gandhamādanaḥ maindaś ca dvividaś caiva suṣeṇo jāmbavāṃs tathā
english: Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha, Gandhamādana, Mainda and Dvivida, Suṣeṇa, and likewise Jāmbavān—

sanskrit: ābabhāṣe gajas tatra plaveyaṃ daśayojanam gavākṣo yojanāny āha gamiṣyāmīti viṃśatim
english: Gaja spoke up there: "I can leap ten yojanas." Gavākṣa declared he would travel twenty yojanas.

sanskrit: gavayo vānaras tatra vānarāṃs tān uvāca ha triṃśataṃ tu gamiṣyāmi yojanānāṃ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: The monkey Gavaya then said to those monkeys: "I shall travel thirty yojanas, O leapers."

sanskrit: śarabho vānaras tatra vānarāṃs tān uvāca ha catvāriṃśad gamiṣyāmi yojanānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: The monkey Śarabha then said to those monkeys: "I shall travel forty yojanas—there is no doubt."

sanskrit: vānarāṃs tu mahātejā abravīd gandhamādanaḥ yojanānāṃ gamiṣyāmi pañcāśat tu na saṃśayaḥ
english: The greatly resplendent Gandhamādana said to those monkeys: "I shall travel fifty yojanas—there is no doubt."

sanskrit: maindas tu vānaras tatra vānarāṃs tān uvāca ha yojanānāṃ paraṃ ṣaṣṭim ahaṃ plavitum utsahe
english: The monkey Mainda then said to those monkeys: "I am capable of leaping fully sixty yojanas."

sanskrit: tatas tatra mahātejā dvividaḥ pratyabhāṣata gamiṣyāmi na saṃdehaḥ saptatiṃ yojanāny aham
english: Then the greatly resplendent Dvivida replied there: "I shall travel seventy yojanas—there is no doubt."

sanskrit: suṣeṇas tu hariśreṣṭhaḥ proktavān kapisattamān aśītiṃ yojanānāṃ tu plaveyaṃ plavagarṣabhāḥ
english: Suṣeṇa, foremost among monkeys, declared to those best of monkeys: "I can leap eighty yojanas, O bulls among leapers."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ kathayatāṃ tatra sarvāṃs tān anumānya ca tato vṛddhatamas teṣāṃ jāmbavān pratyabhāṣata
english: While they were speaking thus, honoring them all, then Jāmbavān, the eldest among them, spoke in reply.

sanskrit: pūrvam asmākam apy āsīt kaś cid gatiparākramaḥ te vayaṃ vayasaḥ pāram anuprāptāḥ sma sāmpratam
english: "Formerly we too had some prowess in speed and movement; but now we have reached the far shore of old age."

sanskrit: kiṃ tu naivaṃ gate śakyam idaṃ kāryam upekṣitum yad arthaṃ kapirājaś ca rāmaś ca kṛtaniścayau
english: "Yet in this situation it is not possible to neglect this task for which the king of monkeys and Rāma are both firmly resolved."

sanskrit: sāmprataṃ kālabhedena yā gatis tāṃ nibodhata navatiṃ yojanānāṃ tu gamiṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Know now the movement that is available to me, given the changes of time: I shall travel ninety yojanas—there is no doubt."

sanskrit: tāṃś ca sarvān hariśreṣṭhāñ jāmbavān punar abravīt na khalv etāvad evāsīd gamane me parākramaḥ
english: And Jāmbavān addressed all those foremost monkeys again: "Indeed my prowess in movement was not merely this much—

sanskrit: mayā mahābalaiś caiva yajñe viṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtaḥ pūrvaṃ kramamāṇas trivikramaḥ
english: "In the past, Viṣṇu the eternal, of great might, striding with his three steps at the sacrifice, was circumambulated by me."

sanskrit: sa idānīm ahaṃ vṛddhaḥ plavane mandavikramaḥ yauvane ca tadāsīn me balam apratimaṃ paraiḥ
english: "Now I am old and slow in my leaping; yet in youth at that time my strength was unmatched by any foe."

sanskrit: saṃpraty etāvatīṃ śaktiṃ gamane tarkayāmy aham naitāvatā ca saṃsiddhiḥ kāryasyāsya bhaviṣyati
english: "Now I reckon my capacity for travel to be this much; yet by this alone the full accomplishment of this task will not come about."

sanskrit: athottaram udārārtham abravīd aṅgadas tadā anumānya mahāprājño jāmbavantaṃ mahākapim
english: Then the greatly wise Aṅgada, honoring Jāmbavān the great monkey, spoke words of noble import in reply:

sanskrit: aham etad gamiṣyāmi yojanānāṃ śataṃ mahat nivartane tu me śaktis syān na veti na niścitam
english: "I shall travel this great distance of one hundred yojanas; but whether I have the strength to return is not certain."

sanskrit: tam uvāca hariśreṣṭho jāmbavān vākyakovidaḥ jñāyate gamane śaktis tava haryṛkṣasattama
english: The foremost of monkeys, Jāmbavān, skilled in speech, said to him: "Your capacity for the going is well known, O best of monkeys and bears—

sanskrit: kāmaṃ śatasahasraṃ vā na hy eṣa vidhir ucyate yojanānāṃ bhavāñ śakto gantuṃ pratinivartitum
english: "A hundred thousand yojanas even you are capable of traveling and returning—this is not the point that is spoken of here.

sanskrit: na hi preṣayitā tata svāmī preṣyaḥ kathaṃ cana bhavatāyaṃ janaḥ sarvaḥ preṣyaḥ plavagasattama
english: "A master who sends others forth should never himself be sent on a mission; all this company is meant to be sent by you, O best of leapers.

sanskrit: bhavān kalatram asmākaṃ svāmibhāve vyavasthitaḥ svāmī kalatraṃ sainyasya gatir eṣā paraṃtapa
english: "You stand established as our protector in the position of master; a master is the companion of the army—this is the accepted way, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: tasmāt kalatravat tāta pratipālyaḥ sadā bhavān api caitasya kāryasya bhavān mūlam ariṃdama
english: "Therefore, dear one, you must always be guarded like a companion; and moreover, O destroyer of enemies, you are the very root of this enterprise.

sanskrit: mūlam arthasya saṃrakṣyam eṣa kāryavidāṃ nayaḥ mūle hi sati sidhyanti guṇāḥ puṣpaphalādayaḥ
english: "The root of an enterprise must be protected—such is the policy of those skilled in affairs; for when the root endures, its qualities flourish like flowers and fruit.

sanskrit: tad bhavān asyā kāryasya sādhane satyavikramaḥ buddhivikramasaṃpanno hetur atra paraṃtapaḥ
english: "Therefore you, of true valor, endowed with the strength of both intelligence and might, O scorcher of foes, are the cause in the accomplishment of this enterprise.

sanskrit: guruś ca guruputraś ca tvaṃ hi naḥ kapisattama bhavantam āśritya vayaṃ samarthā hy arthasādhane
english: "For you are both elder and the son of an elder to us, O foremost of monkeys; relying on you, we are capable of accomplishing the task."

sanskrit: uktavākyaṃ mahāprājñaṃ jāmbavantaṃ mahākapiḥ pratyuvācottaraṃ vākyaṃ vālisūnur athāṅgadaḥ
english: Then Aṅgada, son of Vālin, the great monkey, replied with these words to the greatly wise Jāmbavān who had spoken:

sanskrit: yadi nāhaṃ gamiṣyāmi nānyo vānarapuṃgavaḥ punaḥ khalv idam asmābhiḥ kāryaṃ prāyopaveśanam
english: "If I shall not go, and no other bull among monkeys will either, then surely what remains for us is once again to sit in fasting unto death.

sanskrit: na hy akṛtvā haripateḥ saṃdeśaṃ tasya dhīmataḥ tatrāpi gatvā prāṇānāṃ paśyāmi parirakṣaṇam
english: "For without fulfilling the command of that wise lord of monkeys, I see no preservation of life even if we were to go there.

sanskrit: sa hi prasāde cātyarthaṃ kope ca harir īśvaraḥ atītya tasya saṃdeśaṃ vināśo gamane bhavet
english: "For that monkey lord is supreme in both grace and in wrath; by transgressing his command, destruction would come upon our going.

sanskrit: tad yathā hy asya kāryasya na bhavaty anyathā gatiḥ tad bhavān eva dṛṣṭārthaḥ saṃcintayitum arhati
english: "Therefore, so that this enterprise does not go otherwise, you who see the purpose clearly are the one who ought to consider this."

sanskrit: so 'ṅgadena tadā vīraḥ pratyuktaḥ plavagarṣabhaḥ jāmbavān uttaraṃ vākyaṃ provācedaṃ tato 'ṅgadam
english: Then that heroic bull among leapers, Jāmbavān, having been answered by Aṅgada, spoke these further words to Aṅgada:

sanskrit: asya te vīra kāryasya na kiṃ cit parihīyate eṣa saṃcodayāmy enaṃ yaḥ kāryaṃ sādhayiṣyati
english: "O hero, nothing of this enterprise of yours shall be lacking; I am about to spur on the one who will accomplish it."

sanskrit: tataḥ pratītaṃ plavatāṃ variṣṭham ekāntam āśritya sukhopaviṣṭam saṃcodayām āsa haripravīro haripravīraṃ hanumantam eva
english: Then that hero among monkeys, approaching the foremost among leapers—renowned, sitting apart at ease—urged on that very hero among monkeys, Hanumān himself.

sanskrit: anekaśatasāhasrīṃ viṣaṇṇāṃ harivāhinīm jāmbavān samudīkṣyaivaṃ hanumantam athābravīt
english: Beholding thus the monkey host of many hundreds of thousands, dejected, Jāmbavān then spoke to Hanumān:

sanskrit: vīra vānaralokasya sarvaśāstravidāṃ vara tūṣṇīm ekāntam āśritya hanuman kiṃ na jalpasi
english: "O hero, O best among all who know the scriptures, O Hanumān—sitting apart in silence, why do you not speak?"

sanskrit: hanuman harirājasya sugrīvasya samo hy asi rāmalakṣmaṇayoś cāpi tejasā ca balena ca
english: "Hanumān, you are the equal of the monkey king Sugrīva, and of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa as well, in splendor and in strength.

sanskrit: ariṣṭaneminaḥ putrau vainateyo mahābalaḥ garutmān iva vikhyāta uttamaḥ sarvapakṣiṇām
english: "The son of Vinatā, the mighty Garuḍa—renowned as the son of Ariṣṭanemi, foremost of all birds—

sanskrit: bahuśo hi mayā dṛṣṭaḥ sāgare sa mahābalaḥ bhujagān uddharan pakṣī mahāvego mahāyaśāḥ
english: "—that great-armed bird of great speed and great renown, I have witnessed many times at the ocean, lifting up serpents with his wings.

sanskrit: pakṣayor yad balaṃ tasya tāvad bhujabalaṃ tava vikramaś cāpi vegaś ca na te tenāpahīyate
english: "Whatever strength he has in his wings, that same strength is yours in your arms; nor does your prowess and speed fall short of his.

sanskrit: balaṃ buddhiś ca tejaś ca sattvaṃ ca harisattama viśiṣṭaṃ sarvabhūteṣu kim ātmānaṃ na budhyase
english: "Strength, wisdom, splendor, and courage, O best of monkeys—you are distinguished above all beings; why do you not know yourself?

sanskrit: apsarāpsarasāṃ śreṣṭhā vikhyātā puñjikasthalā ajñaneti parikhyātā patnī kesariṇo hareḥ
english: "The foremost of apsarās among apsarases, renowned as Puñjikasthalā, known as Añjanā—she became the wife of the monkey Kesarī—

sanskrit: abhiśāpād abhūt tāta vānarī kāmarūpiṇī duhitā vānarendrasya kuñjarasya mahātmanaḥ
english: "—by reason of a curse, dear one, she became a monkey-woman able to take any form, the daughter of Kuñjara, the great-souled lord of monkeys.

sanskrit: kapitve cārusarvāṅgī kadā cit kāmarūpiṇī mānuṣaṃ vigrahaṃ kṛtvā yauvanottamaśālinī
english: "While in her monkey nature, lovely in all her limbs, possessed of the power to change form at will, she once took on a human form, adorned with the glory of supreme youth.

sanskrit: acarat parvatasyāgre prāvṛḍambudasaṃnibhe vicitramālyābharaṇā mahārhakṣaumavāsinī
english: "She roamed upon the summit of a mountain like a rain-cloud of the monsoon season, adorned with varied garlands and ornaments, clothed in the finest linen.

sanskrit: tasyā vastraṃ viśālākṣyāḥ pītaṃ raktadaśaṃ śubham sthitāyāḥ parvatasyāgre māruto 'paharac chanaiḥ
english: "From that wide-eyed one, standing on the mountain's peak, the wind gently carried away her golden garment trimmed in red, fair to behold.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa tatas tasyā vṛttāv ūrū susaṃhatau stanau ca pīnau sahitau sujātaṃ cāru cānanam
english: "Then he saw her rounded, well-formed thighs, her full and close-set breasts, and her well-formed, beautiful face.

sanskrit: tāṃ viśālāyataśroṇīṃ tanumadhyāṃ yaśasvinīm dṛṣṭvaiva śubhasarvāgnīṃ pavanaḥ kāmamohitaḥ
english: "Beholding her with broad and ample hips, slender-waisted, of good renown, beautiful in every limb, the Wind God was overcome by desire.

sanskrit: sa tāṃ bhujābhyāṃ pīnābhyāṃ paryaṣvajata mārutaḥ manmathāviṣṭasarvāṅgo gatātmā tām aninditām
english: "Pervaded through every limb by the god of love, his mind undone, Māruta embraced that blameless one with his two mighty arms.

sanskrit: sā tu tatraiva saṃbhrāntā suvṛttā vākyam abravīt ekapatnīvratam idaṃ ko nāśayitum icchati
english: "But she, confused and virtuous, spoke these words right there: 'Who wishes to destroy this my vow of fidelity to one husband?'

sanskrit: añjanāyā vacaḥ śrutvā mārutaḥ pratyabhāṣata na tvāṃ hiṃsāmi suśroṇi mā bhūt te subhage bhayam
english: "Having heard the words of Añjanā, Māruta replied: 'I do not violate you, O fair-hipped one—let there be no fear for you, O fortunate one.

sanskrit: manasāsmi gato yat tvāṃ pariṣvajya yaśasvini vīryavān buddhisaṃpannaḥ putras tava bhaviṣyati
english: "'It is only in mind that I have gone to you; by embracing you, O renowned one, a son endowed with valor and wisdom shall be born to you.'

sanskrit: abhyutthitaṃ tataḥ sūryaṃ bālo dṛṣṭvā mahāvane phalaṃ ceti jighṛkṣus tvam utplutyābhyapato divam
english: "Then as a child, beholding the risen sun in the great forest and wishing to seize it thinking it a fruit, you leaped up and flew toward the sky.

sanskrit: śatāni trīṇi gatvātha yojanānāṃ mahākape tejasā tasya nirdhūto na viṣādaṃ tato gataḥ
english: "Having traveled three hundred yojanas, O great monkey, scorched by the sun's radiance, yet you fell into no despair.

sanskrit: tāvad āpatatas tūrṇam antarikṣaṃ mahākape kṣiptam indreṇa te vajraṃ krodhāviṣṭena dhīmatā
english: "Even as you were rushing swiftly through the atmosphere, O great monkey, the wise Indra, seized with rage, hurled his thunderbolt at you.

sanskrit: tataḥ śailāgraśikhare vāmo hanur abhajyata tato hi nāmadheyaṃ te hanumān iti kīrtyate
english: "Thereupon the left side of your jaw broke against a mountain's rocky peak—and from that very circumstance your name is celebrated as 'Hanumān.'

sanskrit: tatas tvāṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā vāyur gandhavahaḥ svayam trailokye bhṛśasaṃkruddho na vavau vai prabhañjanaḥ
english: "Then, seeing you struck down, the Wind God Vāyu himself, the bearer of fragrance, became greatly enraged and ceased to blow in all three worlds.

sanskrit: saṃbhrāntāś ca surāḥ sarve trailokye kṣubhite sati prasādayanti saṃkruddhaṃ mārutaṃ bhuvaneśvarāḥ
english: "And all the gods, dismayed, the lords of the worlds, when the three worlds were thrown into confusion, sought to appease the enraged Māruta.

sanskrit: prasādite ca pavane brahmā tubhyaṃ varaṃ dadau aśastravadhyatāṃ tāta samare satyavikrama
english: "When the Wind was appeased, Brahmā granted you a boon: that in battle, O dear one, O man of true valor, you would be invulnerable to any weapon.

sanskrit: vajrasya ca nipātena virujaṃ tvāṃ samīkṣya ca sahasranetraḥ prītātmā dadau te varam uttamam
english: "And seeing you unharmed by the fall of his thunderbolt, the thousand-eyed Indra, gladdened in his heart, granted you an excellent boon:

sanskrit: svacchandataś ca maraṇaṃ te bhūyād iti vai prabho sa tvaṃ kesariṇaḥ putraḥ kṣetrajo bhīmavikramaḥ
english: "'May death come to you only at your own free will,' he declared, O lord. You are the son of Kesarī, born of the field, of terrible valor—

sanskrit: mārutasyaurasaḥ putras tejasā cāpi tatsamaḥ tvaṃ hi vāyusuto vatsa plavane cāpi tatsamaḥ
english: "—the legitimate son of Māruta and equal to him in splendor; you are indeed the son of Vāyu, dear one, and his equal in leaping as well.

sanskrit: vayam adya gataprāṇā bhavān asmāsu sāmpratam dākṣyavikramasaṃpannaḥ pakṣirāja ivāparaḥ
english: "We today are as if our life-force is gone; you at this time among us are endowed with skill and valor—like another king of birds.

sanskrit: trivikrame mayā tāta saśailavanakānanā triḥ saptakṛtvaḥ pṛthivī parikrāntā pradakṣiṇam
english: "At the time of Viṣṇu's three strides, dear one, I myself circumambulated the earth with its mountains, forests, and groves, twenty-one times in circumambulation.

sanskrit: tadā cauṣadhayo 'smābhiḥ saṃcitā devaśāsanāt niṣpannam amṛtaṃ yābhis tadāsīn no mahad balam
english: "At that time we gathered medicinal herbs by divine command, from which the nectar was produced—and by that our great strength was born.

sanskrit: sa idānīm ahaṃ vṛddhaḥ parihīnaparākramaḥ sāmprataṃ kālam asmākaṃ bhavān sarvaguṇānvitaḥ
english: "Now I am old, my prowess diminished; at this present time you are the one among us endowed with all virtues.

sanskrit: tad vijṛmbhasva vikrāntaḥ plavatām uttamo hy asi tvadvīryaṃ draṣṭukāmeyaṃ sarvā vānaravāhinī
english: "Therefore, O heroic one, rouse yourself—for you are the greatest among leapers; this entire monkey army desires to witness your valor.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha hariśārdūla laṅghayasva mahārṇavam parā hi sarvabhūtānāṃ hanuman yā gatis tava
english: "Rise, O tiger among monkeys; leap across the great ocean! For your course, O Hanumān, is beyond that of all beings.

sanskrit: viṣāṇṇā harayaḥ sarve hanuman kim upekṣase vikramasva mahāvego viṣṇus trīn vikramān iva
english: "All the monkeys are dejected—O Hanumān, why do you disregard them? Exert your prowess, O greatly swift one, as Viṣṇu exerted his three strides!"

sanskrit: tatas tu vai jāmbavatābhicoditaḥ pratītavegaḥ pavanātmajaḥ kapiḥ praharṣayaṃs tāṃ harivīra vāhinīṃ cakāra rūpaṃ mahad ātmanas tadā
english: Then, spurred on by Jāmbavān, the son of the Wind God, the monkey of renowned speed, gladdening that army of monkey heroes, assumed a great form of his own.

sanskrit: saṃstūyamāno hanumān vyavardhata mahābalaḥ samāvidhya ca lāṅgūlaṃ harṣāc ca balam eyivān
english: As Hanumān was being praised, the mighty one grew in stature; whirling his tail in joy, he attained his full strength.

sanskrit: tasya saṃstūyamānasya sarvair vānarapuṃgavaiḥ tejasāpūryamāṇasya rūpam āsīd anuttamam
english: While he was being extolled by all the bull-like monkeys, filling with his own splendor, his form became matchless.

sanskrit: yathā vijṛmbhate siṃho vivṛddho girigahvare mārutasyaurasaḥ putras tathā saṃprati jṛmbhate
english: As a lion fully grown stretches himself in a mountain cave, so now did the true son of Māruta stretch himself.

sanskrit: aśobhata mukhaṃ tasya jṛmbhamāṇasya dhīmataḥ ambarīṣopamaṃ dīptaṃ vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ
english: The face of that wise one as he stretched shone forth—blazing like a sacrificial vessel, like a smokeless fire.

sanskrit: harīṇām utthito madhyāt saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ abhivādya harīn vṛddhān hanumān idam abravīt
english: Rising from the midst of the monkeys, his body hair standing up in joy, Hanumān bowed to the elder monkeys and spoke these words:

sanskrit: arujan parvatāgrāṇi hutāśanasakho 'nilaḥ balavān aprameyaś ca vāyur ākāśagocaraḥ
english: "Anila, companion of fire, who splinters mountain peaks, the powerful and immeasurable Wind moving through the sky—

sanskrit: tasyāhaṃ śīghravegasya śīghragasya mahātmanaḥ mārutasyaurasaḥ putraḥ plavane nāsti me samaḥ
english: "—I am the true son of that swift-moving, swiftly going, great-souled Māruta; in leaping there is none equal to me.

sanskrit: utsaheyaṃ hi vistīrṇam ālikhantam ivāmbaram meruṃ girim asaṃgena parigantuṃ sahasraśaḥ
english: "I am capable of circling Mount Meru—that vast mountain that seems to scratch the sky—thousands of times without obstruction.

sanskrit: bāhuvegapraṇunnena sāgareṇāham utsahe samāplāvayituṃ lokaṃ saparvatanadīhradam
english: "By the force of my arms' speed I am capable of flooding the entire world—mountains, rivers, and pools—with the sea.

sanskrit: mamorujaṅghāvegena bhaviṣyati samutthitaḥ saṃmūrchitamahāgrāhaḥ samudro varuṇālayaḥ
english: "By the speed of my thighs and legs, the ocean—abode of Varuṇa—will rise up, its great sea monsters thrown into confusion.

sanskrit: pannagāśanam ākāśe patantaṃ pakṣisevitam vainateyam ahaṃ śaktaḥ parigantuṃ sahasraśaḥ
english: "I am capable of circling Vainateyā—the devourer of serpents, flying through the sky, lord of birds—thousands of times.

sanskrit: udayāt prasthitaṃ vāpi jvalantaṃ raśmimālinam anastamitam ādityam abhigantuṃ samutsahe
english: "I am eager even to reach the blazing, ray-garlanded sun as it departs from its rising, before it has set.

sanskrit: tato bhūmim asaṃspṛśya punar āgantum utsahe pravegenaiva mahatā bhīmena plavagarṣabhāḥ
english: "And then I am capable of returning without touching the earth, by that very great and terrible speed, O bulls among leapers.

sanskrit: utsaheyam atikrāntuṃ sarvān ākāśagocarān sāgaraṃ kṣobhayiṣyāmi dārayiṣyāmi medinīm
english: "I am capable of surpassing all beings that move through the sky; I shall churn the ocean and split the earth asunder.

sanskrit: parvatān kampayiṣyāmi plavamānaḥ plavaṃgamāḥ hariṣye coruvegena plavamāno mahārṇavam
english: "As I leap, O leapers, I shall shake the mountains; and leaping with great speed I shall sweep across the great ocean.

sanskrit: latānāṃ vīrudhāṃ puṣpaṃ pādapānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ anuyāsyati mām adya plavamānaṃ vihāyasā bhaviṣyati hi me panthāḥ svāteḥ panthā ivāmbare
english: "The blossoms of creepers, plants, and trees of every kind shall follow after me today as I leap through the sky; my path shall be like the path of Svāti through the heavens.

sanskrit: carantaṃ ghoram ākāśam utpatiṣyantam eva ca drakṣyanti nipatantaṃ ca sarvabhūtāni vānarāḥ
english: "O monkeys, all beings will watch me moving through the terrible sky, soaring upward, and descending.

sanskrit: mahāmerupratīkāśaṃ māṃ drakṣyadhvaṃ plavaṃgamāḥ divam āvṛtya gacchantaṃ grasamānam ivāmbaram
english: "Behold me, O leapers, resembling the great Meru, covering the heavens as I go, as though swallowing the sky.

sanskrit: vidhamiṣyāmi jīmūtān kampayiṣyāmi parvatān sāgaraṃ kṣobhayiṣyāmi plavamānaḥ samāhitaḥ
english: "I shall scatter the clouds, I shall shake the mountains, I shall churn the ocean as I leap, composed and intent.

sanskrit: vainateyasya vā śaktir mama vā mārutasya vā ṛte suparṇarājānaṃ mārutaṃ vā mahābalam na hi bhūtaṃ prapaśyāmi yo māṃ plutam anuvrajet
english: "Whether the power of Vainateyā or my own or that of the mighty Māruta—apart from Suparṇa king of birds or the greatly powerful Wind, I see no being who could follow me once I have leaped.

sanskrit: nimeṣāntaramātreṇa nirālambhanam ambaram sahasā nipatiṣyāmi ghanād vidyud ivotthitā
english: "In the mere twinkling of an eye I shall suddenly fall upon the supportless sky, like lightning rising from a cloud.

sanskrit: bhaviṣyati hi me rūpaṃ plavamānasya sāgaram viṣṇoḥ prakramamāṇasya tadā trīn vikramān iva
english: "As I leap across the ocean, my form shall be like that of Viṣṇu as he strode out his three great strides.

sanskrit: buddhyā cāhaṃ prapaśyāmi manaś ceṣṭā ca me tathā ahaṃ drakṣyāmi vaidehīṃ pramodadhvaṃ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: "I see it clearly in my mind, and my mind's movement accords with it: I shall behold Vaidehī—rejoice, O leapers!

sanskrit: mārutasya samo vege garuḍasya samo jave ayutaṃ yojanānāṃ tu gamiṣyāmīti me matiḥ
english: "Equal to Māruta in speed, equal to Garuḍa in swiftness—my resolve is to travel ten thousand yojanas.

sanskrit: vāsavasya savajrasya brahmaṇo vā svayambhuvaḥ vikramya sahasā hastād amṛtaṃ tad ihānaye laṅkāṃ vāpi samutkṣipya gaccheyam iti me matiḥ
english: "I could suddenly seize the nectar from the hand of Vāsava with his thunderbolt, or from Brahmā the self-born, and bring it here; or I could lift up Laṅkā itself and carry it away—such is my resolve.

sanskrit: tam evaṃ vānaraśreṣṭhaṃ garjantam amitaujasaṃ uvāca parisaṃhṛṣṭo jāmbavān harisattamaḥ
english: To that foremost of monkeys, roaring thus, of immeasurable might, the best of monkeys, Jāmbavān, spoke with great joy:

sanskrit: vīra kesariṇaḥ putra vegavan mārutātmaja jñātīnāṃ vipulaṃ śokas tvayā tāta praṇāśitaḥ
english: "O hero, O son of Kesarī, O swift one, O son of Māruta—by you, dear one, the great grief of your kinsmen has been destroyed.

sanskrit: tava kalyāṇarucayaḥ kapimukhyāḥ samāgatāḥ maṅgalaṃ kāryasiddhyarthaṃ kariṣyanti samāhitāḥ
english: "The foremost monkeys, devoted to your welfare, have assembled; intent, they will perform auspicious rites for the accomplishment of the task.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇāṃ ca prasādena kapivṛddhamatena ca gurūṇāṃ ca prasādena plavasva tvaṃ mahārṇavam
english: "By the grace of the sages, by the counsel of the elder monkeys, and by the grace of your teachers—leap now across the great ocean.

sanskrit: sthāsyāmaś caikapādena yāvadāgamanaṃ tava tvadgatāni ca sarveṣāṃ jīvitāni vanaukasām
english: "We shall stand on one foot awaiting your return; the very lives of all the forest-dwellers are bound up in you.

sanskrit: tatas tu hariśārdūlas tān uvāca vanaukasaḥ neyaṃ mama mahī vegaṃ plavane dhārayiṣyati
english: Then that tiger among monkeys said to those forest-dwellers: "This earth will not bear the speed of my leaping—

sanskrit: etāni hi nagasyāsya śilāsaṃkaṭaśālinaḥ śikharāṇi mahendrasya sthirāṇi ca mahānti ca
english: "—but these peaks of this mountain Mahendra, dense with rocks, firm and great,

sanskrit: etāni mama niṣpeṣaṃ pādayoḥ patatāṃ varāḥ plavato dhārayiṣyanti yojanānām itaḥ śatam
english: "—these shall bear the pressure of my feet as I launch forward, O best ones, and I shall leap a hundred yojanas from this place."

sanskrit: tatas tu mārutaprakhyaḥ sa harir mārutātmajaḥ āruroha nagaśreṣṭhaṃ mahendram arimardanaḥ
english: Then that monkey, resembling the Wind, the son of the Wind God, the destroyer of enemies, ascended the finest of mountains, Mahendra.

sanskrit: vṛtaṃ nānāvidhair vṛkṣair mṛgasevitaśādvalam latākusumasaṃbādhaṃ nityapuṣpaphaladrumam
english: It was covered with trees of many kinds, its meadows frequented by deer, dense with flowering creepers, its trees always in flower and fruit.

sanskrit: siṃhaśārdūlacaritaṃ mattamātaṅgasevitam mattadvijagaṇodghuṣṭaṃ salilotpīḍasaṃkulam
english: It was roamed by lions and tigers, frequented by frenzied elephants, resounding with flocks of excited birds, filled with gushing waters.

sanskrit: mahadbhir ucchritaṃ śṛṅgair mahendraṃ sa mahābalaḥ vicacāra hariśreṣṭho mahendrasamavikramaḥ
english: Mahendra, raised up with great towering peaks—through it that mighty one, foremost of monkeys, whose prowess matched Mahendra's own, ranged about.

sanskrit: pādābhyāṃ pīḍitas tena mahāśailo mahātmanā rarāsa siṃhābhihato mahān matta iva dvipaḥ
english: Pressed down by his two feet, the great mountain, by that great-souled one, roared like a mighty bull elephant struck by a lion.

sanskrit: mumoca salilotpīḍān viprakīrṇaśiloccayaḥ vitrastamṛgamātaṅgaḥ prakampitamahādrumaḥ
english: It released gushing streams of water, its rocks scattered and tumbled, the deer and elephants upon it frightened, its great trees shaking.

sanskrit: nānāgandharvamithunaiḥ pānasaṃsargakarkaśaiḥ utpatadbhir vihaṃgaiś ca vidyādharagaṇair api
english: Pairs of Gandharvas of many kinds, birds rough from intoxication, flocks of Vidyādharas—all took flight,

sanskrit: tyajyamānamahāsānuḥ saṃnilīnamahoragaḥ śailaśṛṅgaśilodghātas tadābhūt sa mahāgiriḥ
english: —as the great mountain's broad plateaus were abandoned, its great serpents lay coiled in hiding, its rocky mountain-peaks and boulders heaved up—such became that great hill.

sanskrit: niḥśvasadbhis tadā tais tu bhujagair ardhaniḥsṛtaiḥ sapatāka ivābhāti sa tadā dharaṇīdharaḥ
english: With those serpents half-emerged and hissing, that bearer of the earth then appeared as if adorned with banners.

sanskrit: ṛṣibhis trāsa saṃbhrāntais tyajyamānaḥ śiloccayaḥ sīdan mahati kāntāre sārthahīna ivādhvagaḥ
english: That rocky height, abandoned by terror-stricken sages who fled in alarm, seemed like a traveler collapsed in a great wilderness, bereft of his caravan.

sanskrit: sa vegavān vegasamāhitātmā haripravīraḥ paravīrahantā manaḥ samādhāya mahānubhāvo jagāma laṅkāṃ manasā manasvī
english: That swift-moving hero among monkeys, his spirit gathered into his speed, slayer of enemy heroes, the great-souled and resolute one—composing his mind, he went toward Laṅkā in his heart.
